name: The Membrane Palette
generated: Do not edit — produced by scripts/build-components.mjs from components/*/

conventions.options: Enumerated options are data-* attributes (data-variant, data-size, data-tone…). Omit the attribute for the default.
conventions.states: Visual states come from native attributes and ARIA (disabled, aria-invalid, aria-selected, aria-current, aria-pressed, aria-busy, open). Set the semantic attribute; never add a state class.
conventions.theming: Dark mode is automatic. Add data-theme="dark"|"light" to any element to force a subtree; add .mp-surface so the subtree paints its own background.
conventions.componentTokens: --mp-<component>-* custom properties are per-component knobs; override them on an instance.
conventions.designTokens: In your own CSS consume semantic tokens (--color-text-*, --color-bg-*, --color-action-*, --space-*, --text-*). Never Tier 1 primitives or raw color values.
conventions.layer: All component CSS is in @layer components; unlayered CSS overrides it.
conventions.behaviorHooks: data-mp-* attributes are hooks for components/membrane.js (e.g. data-mp-toast). Valid on any element.
conventions.tailwind: Using Tailwind v4? Import tokens/membrane-tailwind.css: only mp- utilities exist (bg-mp-surface, text-mp-fg, bg-mp-primary, rounded-mp-lg, shadow-mp-raised, font-mp-display, text-mp-h2); the default palette is removed. p-4 = --space-4.
conventions.patterns: examples/*.html are complete pages (starter, article, dashboard) built only from the library and linted like the examples here.

Do I need a framework?

No. Link one stylesheet and write HTML with mp- classes.

Does dark mode need extra CSS?

No. Every semantic token carries its own light and dark value.

Can agents use it?

Yes — start from components/manifest.json.
